name: Grooming routine (nails, ear/nose hair)
lead: A grooming routine covering nails and ear and nose hair is a set of basic upkeep habits discussed in appearance communities as raising perceived polish. It sits at the line between hygiene and appearance.

Wikipedia lists trimming fingernails and toenails among generally accepted hygiene practices, and distinguishes grooming such as shaving or combing, which supports a good appearance, from hygiene itself.[1] No published study found tests nail or ear and nose hair care for effects on rated attractiveness.
infobox: Nail trimming, ear and nose hair upkeep

paras: Personal hygiene is the set of practices that keep the body clean and healthy, motivated by reducing illness, well-being, social acceptance and avoiding passing illness to others.[1] Standards vary across cultures and change over time.[1]

Wikipedia describes grooming as the practice of cleaning and maintaining parts of the body, and notes a 2007 study by Nelson and Geher in which people who chose their romantic partner reported more mutual grooming, linked to relationship satisfaction and trust.[2] The same article states that the sources it draws on contain little on nails or ear and nose hair specifically.[2]

card.summary: Keeping nails and ear and nose hair tidy; basic upkeep with no attractiveness trials.

quick.overview:
This meta is routine upkeep of details such as nails and ear and nose hair, which proponents say raises how polished someone looks.

References place nail trimming within standard hygiene practice. No study found tests these habits for attractiveness.
quick.mechanism: Tidy small details are said to signal care and cleanliness to observers.
quick.risks: Low risk. Sources reviewed do not describe specific harms.
